statement: A claim that X can never score higher than Y must check every path that moves a criterion out of the denominator, including not-applicable gates, not only the abstention path. Cejel v27 (#442) made A2 abstain on a shallow clone, kept at 0, so a shallow clone would not score above the full clone. But A2's not-applicable gate runs first and itself reads history (git log for .env paths, the history secret scan). A repository whose only A2 surface was a deleted secret-bearing .env became not applicable on a depth-1 or depth-12 clone, left the composite, and scored above the full clone (#556, found reviewing #554). The no-rise test compared rubrics on one clone, never clones under one rubric. Rules: list every exit from the composite (not applicable, self-imposed abstention, unmeasured); for each input an exit reads, ask whether a truncated read can flip it; test the property along the truncated dimension (full vs shallow), not only across rubric versions.

A behaviour fingerprint identifies a rubric's behaviour only over the shapes its corpus holds. Cejel's #556 fix changed v27 scoring on shallow clones, yet v27's pinned fingerprint did not move, because the behaviour corpus has no shallow clone; adding one would have moved every rubric's fingerprint, the calibrated default's included. A review ruling names a candidate by its fingerprint at a commit, so here the fingerprint alone would not tell the old candidate from the new one. Rules: when a scoring change touches a shape the fingerprint corpus lacks, say so in the changelog and name the candidate by commit as well as fingerprint; pin the new shape's scoring surface in its own test, captured from the pre-change scanner, so the change is still caught.

Key an abstention on whether the reads a result relied on completed, not on one cause of incompleteness. Cejel's first #556 fix made v27's A2 abstain on a shallow clone. Review of that fix (#560) found partial clones defeat it: with lazy fetch denied by Cejel's git boundary, history reads on a --filter=blob:none or tree:0 clone failed, the failure went into scanLimitations, and the reader then returned 'nothing found', so A2 scored a warning instead of critical (blobless) or became not applicable (treeless); a git timeout or output-limit overflow fails the same way. Rules: a reader that fails must not return the same value as one that found nothing; the criterion must see the failure, not only the report's limitation list; test the closure along every way a read can be incomplete (truncated, filtered, missing objects, failed), not only the one that was reported.

Never classify a subprocess failure from text that can carry its arguments. Cejel's git wrapper matched patterns such as 'not a git repository', 'timeout' and 'maxBuffer' against stderr plus Node's error.message, and error.message quotes the whole command line, including repository paths (git show <commit>:<path>). The third review of #560 found that a deleted secret in secrets/not a git repository.txt on a blobless clone made the failed read look like 'no repository', which Cejel drops silently, so A2 stayed not applicable and scored above the complete clone under every rubric; a path containing 'timeout' produced a false limit. Rules: classify from fields the runtime and tool control (spawn error code, signal, exit status) and from the tool's own message lines anchored at line start; test with argument text crafted to match each pattern.
